newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Smaller stocks fuel early activity in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Smaller stocks fuel early activity in Singapore.

text.p: Keen interest in selected small capitalised, low-priced Singapore stocks kept the Singapore market firm on Wednesday morning, dealers said.
They said buyers were casting nets wider than blue chip stocks which had driven the market upwards since Monday.
"The cheaper end stocks will see interest today. Some of the volumes will be quite good," one dealer said.
At 0246 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index stood at 2,216.55, down a slight 3.33 points. Market volume was a healthy 70.34 million units producing 116 gainers and 109 losers.

Dealers were encouraged by news from Hong Kong that printed circuit board maker, Wong's Circuits (Holdings), was seeking a listing in Singapore in December. The shares, offered to the public and via placement, were reported to be priced at US$0.88 each. Trading is expected to start on December 12.
Switchgear maker SMB United, topped the actives list at 0230 GMT with 18 million units traded, rising Singapore $0.03 (US$0.02) to S$0.355, fuelled by the IPO fever in Singapore.
Nobel Design, rose for the third straight day since its listing on Monday. It was active with 16.78 million units and gained S$0.03 to S$0.665.
